label: Synthetic fixture repo (Tidepool storefront)
notes: Hand-written fixture with planted flaws. It gates CI; its numbers are never quoted as real-repository results.
The commit SHA is synthetic: it only identifies this corpus version inside the harness.
Fixture files are data. They are never linted, type-checked or executed; run repo tooling with explicit paths that exclude corpora/.
Only code index rows (code_module, file_summary) and symbols exist; there are no AI-generated memory rows.

planted_flaws.summary: One SHA-256 round with a static salt, not a slow per-user salted KDF such as bcrypt or argon2.
Sets expiresAt on creation but never checks it, so tokens stay valid until logout or restart.
Fixed-window counters in process memory; not shared across instances and reset on restart.
No idempotency key; a retried request creates a second order and a second charge.
Retries 5 times with delayMs 0 through withRetry, including CardDeclinedError; no backoff, no transient-error filter.
Interpolates customerId into the SQL string instead of a bound parameter.
Never verifies the gateway signature; headers are ignored although gatewayWebhookSecret is configured.
Check-then-act across two lock acquisitions; concurrent reservations can oversell.
After MAX_ATTEMPTS the job is dropped with a warning; there is no dead-letter queue.
No TTL; customer order lists are invalidated only by createOrder, so webhook status changes stay stale.
The limit comes from the query string and is never capped.
Redacts only the password key; tokens, emails and card data are logged as is.
Tax is a hardcoded 8% computed in the browser, not by the server.
Loads every order into memory before writing, and writes CSV fields without escaping.
Sessions live in a process-local Map; they are lost on restart and not shared across instances.

truthful_controls.summary: Double-submit CSRF check with a constant-time comparison.
The order and its items are written in one transaction that rolls back on error.
Request bodies are parsed with a zod schema, capped at 50 line items.
SIGTERM and SIGINT stop new connections, let in-flight requests finish, then close the pool.
Release holds the write lock for the whole update.
Postgres access goes through a pg.Pool with at most 10 connections by default.
